hints.title: Write the signs before changing inequalities
hints.body: Record the signs of a, b, c and their sums. For each comparison, identify the quantity you will multiply or divide by.
hints.recap: Multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses an inequality.
hints.pitfall: Knowing two quotients are positive does not tell you their order.
hints.pause: Apply the rule to the ordered chain for the product comparison.

recall.reminder: Multiplying or dividing by a negative number reverses an inequality.

hints.title: Check the remaining expressions
hints.body: For a product, work out the sign of each factor separately. For the ratio comparison, compare the numerators first, then divide by their common denominator.
hints.recap: Sign checks and order comparisons are separate calculations.
hints.pitfall: Use the given strict ordering for all allowed triples, not just a chosen example.
hints.pause: Combine the three conclusions and choose the matching row.

recall.reminder: Sign checks and order comparisons are separate calculations.

solution:
I: multiply a<b<c by the negative number a, obtaining a2>ab>ac. This is exactly ac<ab<a2, so I is true.

II: a+c<0 and b<0, so b(a+c)>0. Thus II is true.

III: c>a, but dividing by b<0 gives cb<ab, the opposite of the proposed statement. Thus III is false.

I and II only: E.
knowledgePattern: Propagate a strict negative ordering through products and quotients
